pr_title: [Speculative Decoding 1/2 ] Add typical acceptance sampling as one of the sampling techniques in the verifier
pr_body:
FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE

FIX #5015  (*link existing issues this PR will resolve*)

In this PR we implement typical acceptance sampling as one of the alternate sampling techniques for the Speculative Decoding verifier. In this sampling we do the following

1. For every draft token we compare its probability in the target probability distribution with the entropy of the target distribution and if it meets the acceptance criteria then we accept it. More details on the acceptance criteria can be found in section 3.3.1 in this paper (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.10774)
2. We stop at the first token that is rejected and return
3. If no draft tokens are accepted  then we use greedy sampling to sample a token from the target distribution corresponding to k = 0. The paper also specifies sampling as the fallback option in case no draft tokens are selected
4.  If all the draft tokens are selected then we append the bonus token to the end. The Medusa paper does not talk about the bonus token optimization. However we accept the bonus token since it is drawn from the same target distribution that we are using for accepting the rest of the tokens.

In this PR we make the following changes
1. Add typical_acceptance_sampler.py which implements the sampling logic described above. Also added test cases for the new sampler.
2. Create a base class spec_decode_base_sampler.py to be used by both the rejection_sampler and the new typical_acceptance_sampler.
3. Move some of the logic from rejection_sampler into spec_decode_base_sampler such that it can be used by both the samplers.

As part of this PR we introduce the new sampler. We will hook it up into the spec_decode_worker in a later pr

issue_context.title: [Help wanted] [Spec decode]: Increase acceptance rate via Medusa's typical acceptance
issue_context.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Speculative decoding allows emitting multiple tokens per sequence by speculating future tokens, scoring their likelihood using the LLM, and then accepting each speculative token based on its likelihood. This process is laid out in the following diagram:
![Screenshot 2024-05-23 at 1 45 16 PM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/assets/950914/52d21c58-1a0e-4a8f-b1f8-4abe79651588)

The problem with rejection sampling is that it holds a very high bar for quality: it is lossless and guarantees the distribution of the target model, even if it means rejecting plausible speculative tokens.

This issue is a request to implement Medusa's typical acceptance routing in vLLM. Typical acceptance trades off output quality to increase the acceptance rate. See "Choice of threshold in typical acceptance" in the [Medusa blogpost](https://sites.google.com/view/medusa-llm) for more information.

vLLM users should be able to toggle between different acceptance routines; they can use rejection sampling for tasks that require higher quality, or typical acceptance when speedup is more important.

NOTE: This acceptance routine should work with other proposal types (Eagle, draft, ngram, other), not just Medusa. The speculative decoding framework in vLLM may need improvements to the rejection sampling interface to support this.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

vLLM's rejection sampler is implemented here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/rejection_sampler.py
